title: Set ripple-tank barriers for a two-slit demo: two centred slits, sealed at the walls
instruction: Set up the ripple tank for the two-slit demonstration: stand the three black barrier bars in one straight line across the tank, parallel to the white dipper and 120 mm beyond it (centre line to centre line), closed against both side walls, so that they leave two slits about 15 mm wide, 45 mm apart centre to centre, centred on the tank.
context: School and college science technicians prepare the practical and demonstration set-ups that teachers use, before the lesson. The ripple tank is the standard demonstration of wave interference: a vibrating straight dipper sends plane waves across shallow water toward a barrier with two slits, and a lamp above projects the pattern onto a screen below. For a clean two-slit pattern the barrier pieces go in one straight line across the tank, parallel to the dipper so that both slits are driven in step, closed against both side walls so that no wave leaks round the ends, leaving two slits about one wavelength wide (10 to 20 mm at the usual dipper frequencies) a few wavelengths apart and centred, so the pattern is symmetric and falls in the middle of the screen. A gap at a wall, unequal or off-centre slits, or a barrier at an angle wash out or shift the pattern, so the technician checks the line with a rule before switching on.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Five kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Ripple tank, fixed to the table: a floor of clear acrylic over a white screen sheet (pale blue-white), 260 mm (along x) by 200 mm and 3 mm thick, lying on the table from x 15.0 to 41.0 cm and y -10.0 to +10.0 cm, inside four grey PVC walls 8 mm thick and 15 mm tall (12 mm above the floor). The two side walls run along x from x 15.0 to 41.0 cm with their inside faces at y +10.0 cm and -10.0 cm; the near and far end walls run along y, 216 mm long (across both side walls' ends), with their inside faces at x 15.0 cm and 41.0 cm. Inside, the tank is 260 x 200 mm; it holds no water (see fidelity). (2) Dipper: a fixed white plastic bar, 10 mm (along x) by 180 mm (along y) and 12 mm tall, lying on the tank floor centred at x 18.0 cm, y 0. (3) Beach: a fixed strip of grey foam, 25 mm (along x) by 200 mm and 6 mm thick, on the floor along the far wall (x 38.5 to 41.0 cm). (4) Two long barrier bars: loose black-painted aluminium bars, 70 mm long, 20 mm thick and 25 mm tall, 95 g each, plain rectangular blocks with flat faces. Each stands on the table on a 70 x 20 mm face with its length along y: bar A centred at x 22.0 cm and y +24.0 cm (in front of the left arm), bar B at x 22.0 cm and y -24.0 cm (in front of the right arm). (5) Short barrier bar C: the same but 30 mm long, 41 g, standing the same way centred at x 14.0 cm and y +20.0 cm. A bar's two long narrow faces are alike, and so are its two ends. The bars' lengths add up to 170 mm, so in a line across the 200 mm tank they leave 30 mm of openings: with the long bars closed against the side walls and the short bar in the middle, two slits of 15 mm whose centres are 45 mm apart. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged on the end state from the three bars' poses (in a real trial: a steel rule laid along the line and a photo from above). A bar's 'outline' is its shadow seen from above. A bar 'stands' when its lowest point is within 2 mm of the tank floor's top, its 25 mm side is within 10 degrees of vertical (either way up), and its outline is inside the tank's inside faces (3 mm allowed for contact with a wall, so a bar propped on a wall's top does not stand). The bars form the 'line' when all three stand, each one's length seen from above is within 5 degrees of y (across the tank, parallel to the dipper), their centres are within 6 mm of each other along x, and each centre is 110 to 130 mm beyond the dipper's centre line (x 29.0 to 31.0 cm). Taken in order across the tank by their centres, the bars leave four openings, each measured along y between outlines: the left wall gap (from the left wall's inside face to the nearest bar), slit 1, slit 2 and the right wall gap; bars that touch leave a slit of 0. A slit's centre is the point midway between its two edges. Score 0 if the bars do not form the line (a bar missing, outside the tank, on the table, lying on a side or an end, more than 2 mm above the floor, tilted more than 10 degrees, turned more than 5 degrees, or out of line). Otherwise 0.25, plus 0.25 for each of: (S) both slits 10 to 20 mm wide; (C) the two slits' centres 40 to 50 mm apart, and the point midway between them within 5 mm of the tank's centre line (y 0); (W) both wall gaps 5 mm or less. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Examples: 1.0 with both long bars 1 mm from their walls and the short bar centred (slits 14 mm, centres 44 mm apart); 0.75 (no W) with bar A 6 mm off its wall, bar B against its wall and the short bar 3 mm right of centre (slits 12 and 12 mm); 0.75 (no S) with the long bars against the walls and the short bar 6 mm left of centre (slits 9 and 21 mm); 0.75 (no C) with the short bar against a wall and a long bar in the middle (two 15 mm slits whose centres are 85 mm apart); 0.5 (S and W missed) with bar A 6 mm off its wall, bar B against its wall and the short bar 4 mm left of centre (slits 5 and 19 mm); 0.25 with both long bars 10 mm off their walls (slits 5 mm, centres 35 mm apart). Any bar may go in any place. Limits are inclusive. The score is read at the last step: the trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held for 2.5 s with neither end of any bar moving more than 2 mm in the last 0.5 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit.
fidelity: No water, waves, dipper motor or lamp: the tank is dry and the dipper is a fixed bar. Barriers stand on the floor where they would in a filled tank (they are taller than the water is deep), so real trials are run dry too, with nothing powered or wet near the arms. A small bench tank, 200 mm wide inside. Rigid boxes, the simulator's default friction; tank, dipper and beach fixed. The scorer reads only the bars, so a bar held still within 2 mm of the floor counts as standing.
reset_notes: Stand the three bars back on the table on a long narrow face, lengths along y: long bar A centred at x 22.0 cm and y +24.0 cm, long bar B at x 22.0 cm and y -24.0 cm, and short bar C at x 14.0 cm and y +20.0 cm. The tank, dipper and beach are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
